rule: Every chapter exists because a concrete unresolved fact, obligation or consequence from the previous chapter forces it to exist. Character introduction is subordinate to causality.

chapters.live_problem: a low-risk list contains an obviously suspicious record, an old version ran, the list was operationally exported, and a leaked screenshot predates the batch currently being investigated
must_change: an anomaly becomes an institutional incident
setups: leaked screenshot timestamp 23:46 vs current batch 23:51
director insists on facts before conclusions
chapters.exit_force: freeze all overnight batches and reconstruct which version produced each one

chapters.why_this_actor_enters: the frozen batch logs sit on the technical/vendor side; Luo cannot reconstruct deployment history alone
chapters.live_problem: the team discovers more than one overnight run and must establish whether the older version appeared once or repeatedly
payoffs: screenshot predates current batch -> earlier run must exist
old-version setup begins to acquire a concrete deployment path
new_setups: one configuration fallback occurred after a failed update
a manual rerun was performed by someone before midnight
Zhou's logs show the technical system recorded the rerun but not the human reason
chapters.character_pressure: Zhou becomes useful because his habit of preserving logs matters; he is immediately tempted to take ownership of everything because others are slower
chapters.exit_force: the manual rerun requires finding who requested it and what data snapshot they used

chapters.live_problem: an apparently simple technical rerun turns out to have been requested to meet an operational deadline after a late data update
payoffs: manual rerun setup -> identifies a real human decision under deadline
hospital export setup -> explains why the rerun mattered operationally
chapters.why_this_actor_enters: the rerun request passed through a public-institution coordination channel she now works in; she possesses process records but not model details
new_setups: the rerun request did not explicitly specify model version
two institutions interpreted 'rerun with latest data' differently
a message was forwarded without its earlier context
chapters.character_pressure: He Xin sees that a procedure can be formally followed while still transmitting an ambiguous instruction
chapters.exit_force: the first joint meeting must decide what can be stated publicly before the data/model issue is understood

chapters.why_this_actor_enters: the incident now requires an administrative briefing; Gao receives a draft full of incompatible technical claims
chapters.live_problem: turn several uncertain explanations into a report that can be sent upward without lying or creating unnecessary panic
payoffs: director's facts-before-conclusions stance becomes costly because leaders ask for a causal sentence
new_setups: one side wants to call it a version-control incident
one side wants to call it incomplete-data misuse
one side insists model validity is still unknown
Gao removes a sentence that claims the anomaly 'has been fully contained'
chapters.character_pressure: Gao's caution is useful, but every deletion makes the briefing less decisive and increases pressure from above
chapters.exit_force: a model-side technical review is ordered because the administrative explanation cannot choose between data, version and method

chapters.why_this_actor_enters: the investigation needs someone capable of asking whether the statistical assumptions fail even when the correct version and data snapshot are used
chapters.live_problem: the team reruns selected records under the current version; one suspicious pattern survives
payoffs: low-risk incomplete-follow-up row becomes a methodological question rather than merely deployment noise
new_setups: a censoring/follow-up condition differs from the development setting
Tang recognizes a condition close to a failure mode she once studied but cannot yet claim equivalence
the most convenient institutional explanation becomes scientifically weaker
chapters.character_pressure: negative evidence now threatens an externally visible system rather than a private theorem; Tang has incentive to be careful and incentive to minimize the scope
chapters.exit_force: independent replication is demanded before anyone accepts a model-side explanation

chapters.live_problem: Xu can reproduce one anomaly but refuses to certify the institutions' broader preferred conclusion
payoffs: earlier version/data/method hypotheses are separated into claims with different evidence levels
new_setups: one result can be reproduced only with the exact operational snapshot
a second result disappears when a follow-up rule changes
someone asks Xu for a yes/no statement he cannot honestly give
chapters.character_pressure: verification is finally central, but centrality comes with pressure to become an authority beyond his evidence
chapters.exit_force: industry/operational partners need a decision despite incomplete validation

chapters.why_this_actor_enters: the uncertainty must now be translated into an operational decision with a deadline and downstream cost
chapters.live_problem: pause everything, narrow the system to a verified subgroup, or continue with manual review
payoffs: Xu's differentiated evidence becomes a decision input
new_setups: Song proposes a narrow temporary use rule
her fast decision style solves paralysis but may underweight a rare failure mode
the chosen compromise creates a group that now requires manual follow-up
chapters.character_pressure: she must choose without complete certainty and cannot hide behind statistical caveats
chapters.exit_force: the compromise has staffing and responsibility costs; someone must own the manual-review burden

chapters.live_problem: the technically cautious compromise becomes a concrete queue of people, calls, records and responsibility
payoffs: operational use of the list becomes human workload rather than abstract policy
He Xin's process skill and Luo's coordination memory gain real value
the novel reveals that a 'safe' technical decision can shift cost onto lower-power workers
new_setups: manual review capacity is lower than assumed
one institution wants to count a delayed follow-up as completed for reporting purposes
Luo recognizes that the first leaked screenshot still has no identified source
chapters.exit_force: the technical incident has become a political and labor-allocation conflict while the leak remains unresolved

density_rules: Each chapter must pay off at least one prior setup before adding more than two new major setups.
No chapter may introduce a core actor merely for coverage.
Every new core actor enters because the current unresolved problem reaches their role, information or authority.
No technical explanation may end conflict by itself; consequences move through institutions and people.
At least one apparently convincing early explanation must later prove incomplete, but not fraudulent.
The leaked screenshot source cannot be solved until its revelation changes responsibility or character relations; it cannot be a decorative mystery.
